newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi to invest in car project in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi to invest in car project in Italy.

text.p: In the first foray into Italy by a Japanese carmaker, Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Tuesday it would invest 20 billion yen ($166 million) in a project to produce Mitsubishi-brand sports-utility cars in the country.

Under an eight-year agreement with Industrie Pininfarina SpA, Mitsubishi plans to produce a totally new sports-utility car, modelled on those already made by Japan's Toyota Motor Corp and Suzuki Motor Corp, but with the added pizzazz of Italian design.
Pininfarina already produces luxury and sports cars for such European carmakers such as Fiat SpA, Peugeot and Alfa-Lancia Spa, and will advise Mitsubishi on the design.
"I am honoured that Mitsubishi has chosen Pininfarina for its new project," said group chairman Sergio Pininfarina.
Mitsubishi chairman Hirokazu Nakamura said he visited Pininfarina's car factory 30 years ago, and had dreamed ever since of doing business with the Italian company.
"Sergio is a very gifted aerodynamic engineer, and this is why we wanted to pursue this deal," Nakamura said.
The total investment includes the cost of design and development, and the building of moulds and other manufacturing equipment, the official said.
Pininfarina would invest two billion yen ($16.6 million), Mitsubishi said.

The Italian company would produce 35,000 of the vehicles a year for Mitsubishi at a Pininfarina plant, to go on sale in the spring of 1999 through Mitsubishi's European sales network, a Mitsubishi statement said.

Mitsubishi also said that it is aiming to boost its European sales of Mitsubishi-brand cars to 330,000 a year by 2000, from the current 220,000. It said about half the projected sales would be of cars made in Europe.
Mitsubishi's only other European investment is its Dutch unit, NedCar, owned equally by AB Volvo, Mitsubishi and the Dutch government.
The Italian news comes as a welcome bright spot for Mitsubishi, which has been enbroiled in an embarrassing sexual harassment suit in the United States.

Mitsubishi earlier this month made a deal with American civil rights leader Jesse Jackson's Rainbow/PUSH coalition to end a boycott called by Jackson because of a nine-month old sexual discrimination suit filed by female Mitsubishi workers in the United States.

The federal lawsuit filed by female workers at Mitsubishi's Normal, Illinois, plant alleges that many female employees were subjected to sexual harassment that the company did nothing to address. The suit seeks up to $300,000 each for the workers in back pay.
